```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(lubridate)
source("../../R/portal_config.R")
cfg <- portal_cfg
rel <- portal_release
labs <- portal_labels
v2_current <- rel$is_current(cfg)
version <- cfg$previous_release
start_date <- as.Date(cfg$coverage$start)
end_date <- as.Date(cfg$coverage$end)
base_url <- "https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002"

# The download scripts are kept as text files beside this page; the dates of
# the release are filled in here.
fill_dates <- function(path) {
  text <- paste(readLines(path, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
  text <- gsub("@FIRST_MONTH@", format(start_date, "%Y%m"), text, fixed = TRUE)
  text <- gsub("@LAST_MONTH@", format(end_date, "%Y%m"), text, fixed = TRUE)
  text <- gsub("@FIRST_DAY_COMPACT@", format(start_date, "%Y%m%d"), text, fixed = TRUE)
  text <- gsub("@LAST_DAY_COMPACT@", format(end_date, "%Y%m%d"), text, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub("@FIRST_DAY@", rel$day_text(start_date), text, fixed = TRUE)
}
```

This page holds the files of release `r version` of the OPDI data, the
release that came before `r cfg$release`. It explains how the files are
organised, lists every file for download, and describes how the data were
computed.

```{r status}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
if (v2_current) {
  cat("::: {.callout-note appearance=\"simple\"}\n",
      "Release ", version, " is the **previous** release. It is no longer extended. ",
      "For new work, use release ", cfg$release, ": see [Data](index.qmd) and ",
      "[Releases](releases.qmd#moving-from-v0.0.2), which explains how to move code from ",
      "one to the other.\n:::\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("::: {.callout-note appearance=\"simple\"}\n",
      "Release ", version, " is the release available today. Release ", cfg$release,
      ", described in the rest of the Data section, is being produced and will replace it. ",
      "[Releases](releases.qmd) explains what changes.\n:::\n", sep = "")
}
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Coverage:** `r labs$month_range(start_date, end_date)`, a box around Europe | **Last refresh:** `r cfg$refresh_label` | **Version:** `r version`
:::

## What release v0.0.2 contains

Release `r version` has three tables, each split into files of several days:

| Table | One row per | One file per | Download |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flight list | flight | month | [Flight list files](#flight-list-files) |
| Flight events | event | ten days | [Flight events files](#flight-events-files) |
| Measurements | measured value | ten days | [Measurements files](#measurements-files) |

Two tables of open reference data, used to name airports and runways, can be
downloaded from [OurAirports](https://ourairports.com/):
[airports (CSV)](https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/airports.csv)
and [runways (CSV)](https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/runways.csv).

The files are in Parquet, a file format that stores data by column and that
most data tools read. The ten-day files are named after their first day and
the day after their last day: `flight_events_20220101_20220111.parquet` holds
1 to 10 January 2022.

- The **flight list** gives, for each flight, the aircraft address
  (`ICAO24`), the call sign (`FLT_ID`), the date of flight (`DOF`), the
  departure and destination airports (`ADEP`, `ADES`), other possible airports
  (`ADEP_P`, `ADES_P`), data on the aircraft and the first and last time it was
  seen.
- An **event** is a moment in a flight, with a time, a position and an
  altitude in feet. `flight_id` links it to the flight list's `ID`.
- A **measurement** is a value attached to an event: the distance flown
  (`type` = `Distance flown (NM)`) or the time passed (`type` =
  `Time Passed (s)`) since the start of the flight. `event_id` links it to the
  event's `id`.
- The airport and runway tables shown are a selection of the OurAirports
  columns.

The position reports of a flight can be fetched from the OpenSky Network's
historical database with `ICAO24`, the call sign and the time from
`FIRST_SEEN` to `LAST_SEEN`, for example with the tools on the OpenSky
Network's [data tools page](https://opensky-network.org/data/data-tools).

## Download scripts

Each file has its own web address. The patterns are:

```
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/flight_list/flight_list_{YYYYMM}.parquet
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/flight_events/flight_events_{YYYYMMDD}_{YYYYMMDD}.parquet
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/measurements/measurements_{YYYYMMDD}_{YYYYMMDD}.parquet
```

`YYYYMM` is the year and month. For the ten-day files, the first date is the
first day of the period and the second date the day after its last day. The
periods start on `r rel$day_text(start_date)` and follow each other every ten
days.

The two scripts below download every file of the release into a folder
`data/`. Change the dates in `periods` to download less.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}

## Python download script

```{r v002-python-script}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
cat("```python\n", fill_dates("_v002_download_py.txt"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}

```{r v002-r-script}

#| echo: false
cat("```r\n", fill_dates("_v002_download_r.txt"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

:::

## Flight list files {#flight-list-files}

One file per month, from `r format(start_date, "%B %Y")` to
`r format(end_date, "%B %Y")`.

```{r flight-list-files}
#| echo: false
flight_list_entries <- local({
  entries <- c()
  current <- floor_date(start_date, "month")
  while (current <= end_date) {
    name <- paste0("flight_list_", format(current, "%Y%m"), ".parquet")
    entries <- c(entries, paste0(
      "- **", format(current, "%B %Y"), "**: [", name, "](", base_url, "/flight_list/", name, ")"
    ))
    current <- current %m+% months(1)
  }
  paste(entries, collapse = "\n")
})
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}

## Show the flight list files

`r flight_list_entries`

:::

## Flight events files {#flight-events-files}

One file per ten days, from `r rel$day_text(start_date)`.

```{r ten-day-entries}
#| echo: false
ten_day_entries <- function(table) {
  entries <- c()
  current <- start_date
  while (current < end_date) {
    following <- current + 10
    name <- paste0(table, "_", format(current, "%Y%m%d"), "_", format(following, "%Y%m%d"), ".parquet")
    entries <- c(entries, paste0(
      "- **", rel$day_text(current), " to ", rel$day_text(following - 1), "**: [",
      name, "](", base_url, "/", table, "/", name, ")"
    ))
    current <- following
  }
  paste(entries, collapse = "\n")
}
flight_events_entries <- ten_day_entries("flight_events")
measurements_entries <- ten_day_entries("measurements")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}

## Show the flight events files

`r flight_events_entries`

:::

## Measurements files {#measurements-files}

One file per ten days, over the same periods as the flight events.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}

`r measurements_entries`

## How release v0.0.2 was computed

Release `r version` was produced by an earlier version of the OPDI software.
Its methods differ from those described in [Methods](../methods/index.qmd),
which apply to release `r cfg$release`. They are described here so that the
data can be understood.

### Flights and their identifiers

The position reports of the OpenSky Network (state vectors) were grouped by
aircraft address (`icao24`) and call sign. A group was split into separate
flights where two consecutive reports were more than 30 minutes apart, or
more than 10 minutes apart while the aircraft was below 1 km. Each flight got
an identifier made of the SHA-256 hash of the address and call sign, a
sequence number, and the year and month.

### Departure and destination airports

Around every airport, a circle of 30 NM radius was filled with H3 cells of
resolution 7. H3 is a system that divides the Earth into hexagonal cells;
cells of resolution 7 cover about 5 km² each. Only the reports below
4,000 ft were kept. Each report was matched to the airports whose circle
contains its cell. The airport nearest to the first (or last) matching report
became the departure (or destination) airport; the other candidates were
written in `ADEP_P` (or `ADES_P`).

### Flight events

| Event type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `level-start`, `level-end` | Start and end of a level segment. |
| `top-of-climb` | First report of the first cruise phase. |
| `top-of-descent` | Last report of the last cruise phase. |
| `take-off` | First report of the climb phase after a ground phase. |
| `landing` | First report of the ground phase after a descent phase. |
| `first-xing-fl50`, `first-xing-fl70`, `first-xing-fl100`, `first-xing-fl245` | First crossing of flight level 50, 70, 100 or 245. |
| `last-xing-fl50`, `last-xing-fl70`, `last-xing-fl100`, `last-xing-fl245` | Last crossing of that flight level. |
| `entry-runway`, `exit-runway` | Entry into and exit from a runway. |
| `entry-taxiway`, `exit-taxiway` | Entry into and exit from a taxiway. |
| `entry-parking_position`, `exit-parking_position` | Entry into and exit from a parking position (stand). |

The **flight phases** (ground, climb, cruise, level, descent) were found
with the fuzzy logic of OpenAP, an open aircraft performance model by Junzi
Sun of TU Delft. For the flight-level crossings, a smoothed flight level was
computed for each report and compared between consecutive reports. The
airport areas (runways, taxiways, parking positions) came from OpenStreetMap,
filled with H3 cells of resolution 12, and each report was matched to them.
The `info` field of the airport events holds the OpenStreetMap details of the
area, as JSON text.

### Measurements

- **Distance flown (NM)**: the great-circle distance between consecutive
  reports, added up from the first report of the flight, in nautical miles.
- **Time Passed (s)**: the time since the first report of the flight, in
  seconds.

Each event got the two values of the report it was taken from.
